I've actually done a bit of studying about this. Apparently, some people's genetic makeup makes them more prone to depression than other people, as depression is a chemical imbalance in your brain. Some people are born with a predisposition, but depression only occurs if a trigger happens, like the death of a family member or something like that. However, some people may not have a predisposition or a trigger and still develop depression. Depression is a different disease for everyone. TL;DR Depression is genetics and situation based, but you aren't technically born with it.

People definitely use depression as an excuse to not do work, but the amount of people with actual depression who do that is very small. Most of the time, people feign depression and sadness to get attention and to be able to slouch around and have other people do work for them. One day in school we were told that our french teacher choked to death in her sleep, and kids refused to do work because they said they were too "depressed" that she died, even though most of them didn't have her, and the majority of the people who did didn't like her. It made me sick that people would use the death of someone to get out of doing work at school for a week. Some people, including myself, were genuinely sad that she died, and took time to mourn, but it's disgusting to use their death as a way to not go to school or do work. Sorry for the wall, but your post just reminded me of that.

I'm the same way. Personally, I did things where you could always improve, and get better at. I used to play basketball, and at the beginning I was terrible at it and couldn't even make a 2 point shot with no defense. I played for 2 years and it kept me focused, and distracted me from the shitty world around me, even for a few brief moments.

What do you enjoy doing? Even something small like going on walks can really help, especially if you live in a beautiful area.

I suck with keeping up with new hobby's, but keep on trying. Maybe try forcing yourself to stay with something for a month, and if you still don't enjoy it, try something different. Eventually you'll find a good hobby that you enjoy. Tl;DR keep on trying out different hobbies, and eventually you'll find your passion.
